question: Which classification of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) involves narrowing the vaginal opening by cutting and repositioning the labia?
explanation: Type III FGM, also known as infibulation, involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a seal using the labia. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h1)

question: What procedure is performed in Type II FGM that separates it from Type I?

options.A: Excision of the clitoris and the labia minora
options.B: Cauterization of the vaginal wall using heated instruments
options.C: Simple piercing of the prepuce without tissue removal
options.D: Infibulation and creation of a covering seal

explanation: Type II involves removing both the clitoris and the labia minora, whereas Type I involves only the clitoris or its prepuce. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is a major socio-cultural reason why FGM continues to persist in some communities?

options.A: Enhancing natural fertility rates in young women
options.B: Preserving female purity and ensuring marriageability
options.C: Complying with modern international health guidelines
options.D: Preventing the transmission of common bacterial infections

explanation: Traditional societies often link the practice directly to concepts of chastity, honor, and social acceptance for marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why do families often continue the practice of FGM despite legal bans?

options.A: Instructions mandated by orthodox religious leaders nationwide
options.B: Lack of basic understanding regarding female anatomy
options.C: Direct financial incentives provided by government agencies
options.D: Fear of community isolation and severe social stigma

explanation: Deep-rooted cultural expectations make social acceptance a powerful driver that often overrides legal deterrents. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which immediate complication is most likely to happen right after the FGM procedure?
explanation: Cutting the richly vascularized external genitalia often leads to immediate, uncontrolled bleeding and hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a major risk during childbirth for a woman who has a history of Type III FGM?

options.B: Hyperactive uterine contractions in early labor
options.C: Immediate postpartum hemorrhage from placenta accreta
options.D: Prolonged labor and severe perineal tearing

explanation: Dense scar tissue from infibulation creates a mechanical barrier, making fetal descent difficult and leading to prolonged labor and severe tears. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a frequent psychosexual issue reported by survivors of FGM?

options.A: Hyperesthesia of the remaining pelvic tissue
options.C: Complete absence of any psychological trauma

explanation: The removal or scarring of sensitive nerve endings directly contributes to painful intercourse (dyspareunia) and diminished pleasure. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why do many survivors of FGM experience chronic anxiety or post-traumatic stress?

options.A: They suffer from irreversible neurological brain damage
options.B: Modern medications used for treatment cause severe paranoia
options.C: Hormonal imbalances directly alter their cognitive processing
options.D: They vividly recall the terror and severe pain of the procedure

explanation: The physical trauma, often inflicted during childhood without anesthesia, leaves lasting psychological scars that trigger anxiety. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a nurse when assessing an FGM survivor?

options.A: Scolding the family members for allowing the procedure to happen
options.B: Maintaining privacy and approaching the examination with sensitivity
options.C: Immediately reporting the patient to local law enforcement authorities
options.D: Performing surgical de-infibulation immediately without consent

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental environment is crucial for building trust and encouraging patients to share their health history. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which clinical finding suggests a history of FGM during an antenatal booking visit?

options.A: Frequent episodes of painless gestational hypertension
options.B: Enlargement of the clitoral hood and excess tissue folds
options.C: Presence of perineal scar tissue and altered external anatomy
options.D: Complete absence of vaginal secretions and normal pH levels

explanation: Visual inspection revealing missing structures or scar tissue serves as a direct indicator of previous genital cutting. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the term for the surgical opening of infibulated scar tissue?
explanation: De-infibulation is the surgical procedure used to open up fused scar tissue in women with Type III FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h6)

question: When is the best time to perform de-infibulation for a pregnant woman with a complete Type III FGM?

options.A: At six weeks postpartum during the postnatal checkup
options.B: During the first trimester to prevent early miscarriage
options.C: During the first stage of labor or electively before labor
options.D: Immediately after the baby is delivered and placenta removed

explanation: Opening the scar tissue prior to or during early labor prevents severe tearing and allows for a safer delivery. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which Nigerian law explicitly prohibits and penalizes the practice of Female Genital Mutilation?

options.B: Child Rights and Education Protection Code

explanation: The VAPP Act criminalizes FGM at the federal level in Nigeria, providing the legal basis for prosecution. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is an effective way for a clinical nurse to help stop the practice of FGM?

options.A: Reporting every pregnant woman from an endemic tribe to the police
options.B: Providing community health education on the health hazards of the practice
options.C: Performing medicalized FGM secretly in hospitals to prevent infections
options.D: Ignoring the practice to respect cultural autonomy and traditions

explanation: Nurses can drive community-level behavioral change by educating the public on the severe health risks linked to FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h7)
